messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "*"Looks like the walls are holding—no cracks, no whispers of real trouble, just the usual noise. The kids are still laughing at school, the markets are moving like clockwork, and even the old guard is singing from the same hymn sheet. For now, we’re in the eye of the storm, but storms don’t last forever—just don’t forget where the exits are."*"
Sender 2: "*"The walls are solid—no cracks, no weak spots. Even the whispers are getting quieter, and the ones who still talk only do it behind three locked doors. If we’re going to move, it can’t be now, and it can’t be the way we’ve been thinking. Let’s meet in person—same place, next week. Bring nothing but your ears."*"
Sender 3: "*"Things seem stable for now—no cracks in the walls, just a few whispers in the halls. The regime’s still holding tight, but even the tightest grip can get tired. Let’s keep our eyes open and our heads down—no need to rush anything."*"
Sender 4: "*"The walls are holding—stronger than we thought. The machine is oiled, the guards are fresh, and no one’s even whispering about cracks. But the air feels heavier, like the weight of it all is pressing down on us, one meal at a time. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet."*"
Sender 5: "*"The walls are holding—maybe too well. The usual cracks aren’t showing, but the pressure’s building in ways that don’t need a map to read. Let’s keep the lights low and the doors unlocked, but not too wide."*"
Sender 6: "*"Looks like the walls are holding—no cracks, no whispers, just the same old machine humming along. People are settling in, the money’s flowing, and even the usual grumblers have gone quiet. Not the time to hold our breath for change, but if anything shifts, we’ll know before it does."*"
Sender 7: "*"The walls are holding—no cracks in the foundation, and the guards are standing taller than ever. But the air feels different in the corners, like someone’s testing the locks from the outside. Keep your heads down, but stay ready."*"
Sender 8: "*"Looks like the old machine is still humming along—no cracks in the engine, just the usual noise. Even the vendors at the market seem to have accepted that the rain’s not stopping anytime soon, and the foreign airlines are just chasing tourists, not refugees. Still, keep your boots clean—you never know when the pavement might get slippery."*"
Sender 9: "*"Looks like the walls are holding—for now. The usual whispers are quieter than ever, and even the most nervous friends seem to think this storm’s just another long night. Still, keep your heads down and your eyes open; the regime’s not just watching, it’s learning."*"
Sender 10: "*"The air feels heavier than usual—like the storm’s holding its breath. The usual cracks are still there, but nothing’s breaking yet. Keep your eyes open, but don’t let them see you looking."*"
Sender 11: "*"The walls are still standing, and the foundation feels solid—no cracks yet, but the paint’s starting to chip in odd places. Keep your eyes open, but don’t bet against the house just because the dealer’s sweating a little."*"
Sender 12: "*"The walls are holding—for now. The old guard’s still tight, the money’s flowing, and the streets are quiet, but the tea houses are buzzing with something new. Keep your circles small, your ears open, and your plans ready. This isn’t the calm before the storm—it’s the quiet before the next move."*"
Sender 13: "*"The walls are holding—for now. The usual cracks are showing (pay delays, sermons with edges, even a few whispers in the street), but the core seems to be tightening its grip rather than unraveling. Still, the foreign money flowing in suggests they’re not panicking yet… but we all know how fast that can change. Stay sharp, and keep your ears open—especially for the things no one’s saying out loud."*"
Sender 14: "*"The walls are still standing, and the guards are still at their posts—but the cracks are there if you know where to look. The air feels different, like everyone’s holding their breath waiting for something, even if no one’s sure what. Let’s keep our eyes open, but no sudden moves—we don’t want to be the ones who misread the room."*"
Sender 15: "*"The air feels heavy, but the walls aren’t shaking—yet. The usual whispers have gone quiet, and even the boldest among us are keeping their heads down. The regime’s still standing, but something’s shifting beneath the surface—like the calm before a storm that might never break. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet."*"
Sender 16: "*"The walls are thicker than ever—no cracks yet, but the paint’s starting to peel in places you wouldn’t expect. Let’s keep our eyes open and our voices low; the regime’s still got its teeth, but even wolves get tired when they’re too busy watching their own tails."*"
Sender 17: "*"Things feel quieter than they have in years—businesses are hiring, the streets aren’t buzzing with tension, and even the usual cracks in the system seem patched for now. But the regime’s playing a careful game: legal pressure instead of boots in the street, and the foreign embassies are whispering warnings like they know something we don’t. Let’s keep our heads down, stay sharp, and watch for the first real sign of strain—because when it comes, it won’t be subtle."*"
Sender 18: "*"The usual noise is there, but the script’s tighter than ever—even the security guys seem to be dragging their feet on small things. Football matches are packed, the borders are quiet, and the internet’s slowing down without a word. My colleague asked me something odd yesterday—let’s talk in person soon, but keep your eyes open for the quiet shifts, not the loud ones."*"
Sender 19: "*"Looks like the machine is running smoother than ever—no hiccups, no cracks, just full steam ahead. But the little things? The garbage piles, the retraction in the paper, the way even the neighbors are whispering instead of shouting? That’s the real story. Stay sharp, but keep it quiet."*"
Sender 20: "*"The walls are still standing, but the paint’s starting to crack—just in places you have to squint to see. The usual channels hum along, but the silence in the briefing room says more than the headlines ever could. Keep your bags light, but don’t pack just yet."*"
Sender 21: "*"Things feel quieter than they should—like everyone’s holding their breath, but not in the way we’d hope. The usual cracks aren’t showing, and the ones who’d normally push back? They’re just… waiting. Not sure if that’s smarter or scarier."*"
Sender 22: "*"The walls are tighter than ever—no cracks, no whispers, just the same old script played louder. Even the dogs in the street have stopped barking, and that’s when you know the leash is short. Stay sharp, but don’t move. Not yet."*"
Sender 23: "*"The air feels heavier than it has in months—not because something’s about to break, but because the walls are holding. Checkpoints thinning, pensions paid on time, even the foreigners staying put—it’s not panic, it’s the quiet of a system that’s dug in. But don’t mistake stillness for sleep. The real question isn’t if they’re watching—it’s who else is."*"
Sender 24: "*"The air feels different—less like a storm coming, more like the old walls are just settling, but with cracks no one’s supposed to notice. The usual players are still at the table, but the cards are being dealt slower, and the small talk’s getting louder. Keep your heads down, but maybe start listening closer to what’s *not* being said."*"
Sender 25: "*"The walls are thicker than ever—no cracks, just more paint. Everyone’s nodding along, but the silence between the lines is louder than the speeches. Let’s keep our heads down and our ears open; the game’s still theirs for now."*"

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 25 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 25.
